1. Outside view: Biweekly moves in this series are typically ±0.5–1.5 points, with occasional 2.6-point swings (7/15 33.4 → 7/29 30.8). Over 2026 the series has trended up from ~28.5 in April to ~32 in August, i.e. roughly +0.4/release drift, but with clear mean-reverting noise around that trend. Naive extrapolation from 32.3 (last print) with slight upward drift and partial mean reversion toward the last three-print average (32.2) gives ~32.2–32.6.

2. Inside view: Michigan sentiment fell 7.6% in August (51.0 from 55.2) on Middle East conflict/inflation fears, LSEG/Ipsos also fell 1.6 points. That is a real negative signal, worth maybe −0.5 to −0.8 on this index — but the 8/12 CivicScience print (+1.5 to 32.3) already came after that news and rose anyway, so CivicScience's high-frequency panel appears to be diverging from Michigan (it captures markets at record highs, moderating gasoline/oil near $80, improving credit outlook per their Financial Health Index note). Net inside-view adjustment: about −0.4, partly reflecting mean reversion after a +1.5 jump. Also note the series has been capped near 33.4 in 2026; upside above that is less likely.

3. Pre-mortem: Most likely way I'm wrong is a sharp downside break — a war/inflation shock or labor-market deterioration transmitting to the panel with a lag, producing a 30.0–30.5 print (the 7/29 pattern of giving back a rally). Second most likely: continued melt-up to 33.5+. I correct by shading the mean slightly below the last print and keeping the distribution wide with mild left skew, which I express through a somewhat larger sd rather than skew.

4. Calibration: Mean absolute change per release is ~1.0–1.2, sd of changes ~1.2–1.4. So sd ≈ 1.3 around a mean near 31.9 gives ~2/3 coverage in 30.6–33.2, consistent with observed volatility.
